decisions.note: Round 4: maker showed raw URL as the list item's name; client rejected it and specified the reference-correct behavior (show the real page title) instead.

Round 5: maker's 'automatic metadata' decision only ever fetched title, never description/favicon/preview image; client affirmed the auto-naming without noticing the other required fields were absent — satisficing miss.
Round 5: client asked to be able to tweak/rename the auto-generated title, a capability the maker had not yet surfaced (prototype so far had no edit path).
Round 8: maker scoped full-text search to name+address only (no description/note field ever built); client praised address-matching without flagging the narrower-than-reference search scope.

Round 11: duplicate-save handling only flashes/scrolls to the existing bookmark rather than guiding the user into editing it as the reference requires; client called this 'perfect' without noting the missing edit-guidance step.

Round 13 final scope-lock recap (explicit 'anything to add?' gate) never mentions tags, unread/read state, bulk actions, or sorting; client said 'nothing to add,' passing on the chance to extend into these core items.
